newsitem.title: UK: UK superstores beat high street on sales rise.
newsitem.headline: UK superstores beat high street on sales rise.

text.p: Out-of-town superstores accounted for 51 percent of Britain's 8.4 billion stg rise in retail sales last year as consumers continued to buy goods increasingly outside city centres, according to a report released on Monday.
A survey by retail consultants Verdict forecast that the trend would continue, with out-of-town superstores expected to account for a third of all retail sales in 2001, up from 28.7 percent in 1996.
"Superstores will remain the main engine of retail growth over the next five years, increasing the proportion of retail sales that they account for, largely through further expansion," Verdict said.
The group predicted that superstore numbers would grow by a quarter to 6,070 by 2001.

Verdict said it saw evidence of superstore saturation in the grocery, do-it-yourself (DIY) and electricals sectors, while furniture and carpets was an area that was fast switching away from high streets to out-of-town sites.
